facts.claim: Melenos Art Boutique Hotel (in the village of Lindos, Rhodes, next to the Lindos acropolis) says its wedding coordinators can arrange a civil ceremony, a symbolic ceremony or a traditional Orthodox wedding. Once a couple chooses the hotel they receive a detailed schedule of the coming months and a costing sheet setting out the deadlines; the coordinator organises tasks, outlines a budget, builds an itinerary of events, assists throughout planning, meets the couple on arrival and stays with them until the ceremony. Re-check of Greece pack fact_104 and fact_105.

Melenos says its wedding planner takes care of the required legal documentation, including filing documents, marriage licence registration and the government and administrative fees, and official witnesses can be provided on request. (The page says fees exist and that the coordinator attends to them; it does not say whether they sit inside or outside the costing.) Re-check of Greece pack fact_105.

Melenos suggests reserving the entire hotel for a minimum of three nights for a wedding (a suggestion, not stated as a condition); additional guests can stay at the Melenos Apartments and Studios in the village, a 10 minute walk from the hotel. Re-check of Greece pack fact_106.

Melenos coordinators assist with decor (seasonal flowers from the hotel garden or a special order from a local florist; bouquets, corsages, centrepieces; the hotel's own decorative objects), details for Orthodox ceremonies such as Jordan almonds on a silver tray, and the reception menu (traditional Greek with South Mediterranean influences, modified for dietary needs). It lists other services the coordinators can organise as additional services: rehearsal dinner on the Melenos terrace, pre-wedding welcome cocktail party, professional photographer and videographer, hair and make-up artists, private boat excursion, live music, donkeys to carry the couple to the ceremony and a candlelit dinner for the couple after the ceremony. Re-check of Greece pack fact_107.

Angsana Corfu Resort & Spa (Corfu) links a 2026 wedding brochure from its Weddings & Honeymoons page, alongside a real weddings page, a wedding venues page and a wedding proposal request form. Re-check of Greece pack fact_305.

Angsana Corfu's 2026 wedding brochure lists its ceremony venues under the heading 'Symbolic Wedding Ceremony Venues': Vertigo Sky Bar (outdoor, maximum 250, available mid-May to the end of September, weather permitting) and Oribu Garden (outdoor, maximum 30, April to October, weather permitting). Reception venues are Vertigo Sky Bar (outdoor, maximum 250, end of May to end of September, weather permitting), Oribu Restaurant (outdoor and indoor, maximum 150, April, May, September and October) and Oribu Garden (outdoor, maximum 30, April to October). The brochure does not mention civil or Orthodox ceremonies or a package inclusion list.
facts.conflicts: Brochure gives Vertigo Sky Bar availability as 'mid-May' for ceremonies but 'the end of May' for receptions.

facts.claim: Angsana Corfu's 2026 brochure describes a 'Special Wedding Offer': a credit towards a next stay at any Banyan Tree or Angsana hotel, and, for wedding bookings above a stated minimum food and beverage spend, one complimentary night for the couple in a One-Bedroom Sea View Suite or Ionian Sea View Villa with private pool, a welcome amenity (champagne, fruit and traditional sweets) and in-room breakfast the day after the wedding. The amounts are omitted here; the offer is conditional on a minimum food and beverage spend.

Grand Resort Lagonissi (Athens Riviera) says couples can take advantage of the resort's 'exclusive wedding and honeymoon packages', with a stay in a sea view suite, beachfront bungalow or waterfront private villa. The Weddings & Ceremonies page names five venues (Uranus open-air terrace for a 'Grand Wedding Gala', Veghera on the south water edge of the peninsula, La Piscina garden and pool, Aphrodite, Villa Elounda garden near a private sandy beach) but publishes no package inclusion list, conditions or ceremony types. Re-check of Greece pack fact_208.

Grand Resort Lagonissi lists its wedding services as: wedding assistance from its Events team; chefs and pastry chefs for wedding cakes and desserts; private party planning in a suite or by the beachfront; professional designers for flowers and table and venue decoration; DJs with sound and lighting technical support; specialised services such as photography, special effects and limousine rentals; a 'Honeymoon Suite'; bridal treatments and beauty facilities; and dinners by a private pool with a personal chef. It does not say which of these sit inside a package.

Costa Navarino (Messinia, south-west Peloponnese) says traditional religious marriages can be held at the chapel of St Samson within Navarino Dunes or at St Eleni at Navarino Agora, and civil ceremonies can be arranged on request indoors in town halls or outdoors (beach, boat, hilltop, beside a stream). Its weddings page names The Romanos, a Luxury Collection Resort, W Costa Navarino and Mandarin Oriental, Costa Navarino (eight indoor and outdoor spaces from 62 sqm to 868 sqm) and refers to four 5-star resorts; enquiries go through a weddings email and booking calendars. It publishes no wedding package or inclusion list. Re-check of Greece pack fact_209 and fact_210.

Grecotel Corfu Imperial (Kommeno, Corfu) offers weddings and vow renewals with dedicated wedding specialists, customised menus and 'trusted vendors'. Named venues are Yali Waterfront Restaurant on a deck above the water, Aristos Restaurant for up to 50 guests and the private island 'Nissaki' for up to 50 guests; enquiries go through a request for proposal form. The page publishes no package inclusion list, conditions or ceremony types. Re-check of Greece pack fact_108.

Atrium Prestige (south Rhodes) names ceremony and reception venues (Amphitheater a few steps from the beach, described as ideal for larger events; the private Tsambika chapel reached across a bridge, offered 'for a more traditional wedding ceremony'; Lachania private beach; Golden Dome; Panoramic Terrace; Thallassa restaurant for receptions; Kalithea main bar for the party, with fireworks). For couples seeking a civil ceremony, its wedding specialist assists with all arrangements needed to obtain the marriage licence. It also offers symbolic ceremonies, elopements and vow renewals. Re-check of Greece pack fact_307.

Atrium Prestige lists wedding services on its weddings page: bridal suite (a sea view villa with personal pool to get ready in), decoration and flowers, bridal make-up and hairstyling, on-site photographer, bridal bouquet, wedding cake, wedding reception with a menu tasting with the chef, DJ or live music (violin, guitar or bouzouki), fireworks, spa treatments, honeymoon villa, private dinner for two, couple's massage (a complimentary hydrobath for stays of 5 nights and above), a complimentary in-room offer of fruit or sweets with sparkling wine, and a romantic boat trip. It does not group these into a named package or say which carry a charge.

As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens lists among its notarial services witnessing application forms for, and issuing, Certificates of No Impediment (CNI) and witnessing notices of intended marriage, plus legalisation of signatures and seals by authentication or apostille. An appointment is required for all notarial services (Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 12:30pm), although CNI and apostille documents can be submitted by post; CNIs and apostilled documents are available for collection within two working days unless same-day collection has been arranged. The Embassy does not provide legal advice, honorary consuls cannot provide notarial services, notarial service fees apply and an additional fee applies for return by post. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. Re-check of Greece pack fact_212 and Crete pack fact_207.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Getting married overseas' page (last updated 18/08/2026, re-read live 2026-11-11) gives general advice only and says some countries ask you to prove you are not already married, with each country deciding what proof it accepts; the most common documents are a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages. The destination may have further rules, and Smartraveller says it cannot tell you what you will need. DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need one, whether you can get it in Australia and whether it needs an authentication or apostille. Local authorities may also ask for divorce papers, a deceased spouse's death certificate, and an original birth certificate and passport. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. Re-check of Greece pack fact_206 and Crete pack fact_208.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia; a foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of marriage but may not be usable as proof of a name change (check with your local registry); talk to a lawyer to confirm validity. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. Re-check of Greece pack fact_207 and Crete pack fact_209.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's overall advice level for Greece is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (page updated 30 September 2026, still current at 11 November 2026, re-read live 2026-11-11). It says wildfires occur during the extended summer period from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations, prompting evacuations; heatwaves are frequent over the summer months; and Greece is in an active seismic zone. Re-check of Crete pack fact_204 and fact_205.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's Greece page says Australians entering the Schengen area for a short stay (90 days or less) on an Australian passport register biometric details such as fingerprints and a photo on arrival under the EES, need take no action beforehand, pay nothing for EES registration, and may face delays at border crossings; during peak season severe traffic congestion occurs in the main cities and on the islands; and only licensed taxis should be used, with the meter running. Re-check of Crete pack fact_206.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's Greece page says to get comprehensive travel insurance before you leave and closely read the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS); it must cover all medical costs overseas, including evacuation, which the Australian Government will not pay; if you can't afford travel insurance you shouldn't travel. There is no agreement between Australia and Greece for free healthcare, so tourists pay for all medical care, including hospital stays and evacuation, and payment is required before leaving the facility. Check the policy covers the whole trip including stopovers, and know the exclusions (some activities, such as going on a cruise, may cost extra to cover).

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Travel insurance' page (current URL https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/travel-essentials/travel-insurance, last updated 18/08/2026; the old /before-you-go/insurance/travel-insurance URL returns 404) says to always read the PDS before buying (inclusions, exclusions, definitions, claims process, emergency support); choose a policy covering every country including stopovers and transit points; check whether the policy covers cancellations if the advice level goes up after you have booked; insurers exclude many activities from standard policies, even common ones like going on a cruise, so you may need to pay extra; you must declare all pre-existing conditions, and declare everything upfront or you may void the policy; credit card insurance often covers fewer situations and usually has to be activated; basic (medical-only) policies usually don't cover cancellation costs; travel insurance can cover cancellation costs if plans change, so find out what your policy covers before you buy.

Four Seasons Astir Palace Hotel Athens (Vouliagmeni, Athens Riviera) headlines its weddings page 'Luxury Greece Wedding Packages in Athens' and says it provides complete event coordination for ceremonies and receptions; couples reserve exclusive waterfront venues across its 30-hectare (75-acre) estate for 10 to 1,000 guests; its event specialists manage banquet menus, seating and guest room blocks; options range from a single-day ceremony to a three-day destination itinerary with spa treatments and private beach access; it has an in-house wedding planner and offers vow renewals. Re-check of Greece pack fact_200 and fact_201.

Amanzoe (Kranidi, east Peloponnese) says on its celebrations page that it hosts weddings of all sizes with personalised experiences and invites couples to contact it for a full proposal ('from conception through to execution'). It publishes no wedding package, inclusion list, conditions or ceremony types.

Four Seasons Astir Palace Athens publishes 'Wedding Inclusions' that couples who book a wedding receive: one night of accommodation (the wedding night) for the couple; tailor-made amenities on the wedding night; a designed menu tasting for up to four guests; planning assistance from a dedicated in-house wedding specialist; a dedicated service team on the day; choice of venues; premium tables, chairs and linens; Sambonet silver and Rosenthal fine bone china; high-speed internet throughout the stay; and access to waterfront and garden locations as photography backdrops. It does not state ceremony types or a minimum guest count.

Four Seasons Astir Palace Athens says its on-site wedding specialist works 'with you or your consultant' to reserve dates, plan the schedule, coordinate food and beverage and assist with other arrangements; the team can arrange flowers with its preferred floral designers or work with the florist of the couple's choice; it can provide a list of recommended vendors such as photographers and entertainers; local transport for the couple or guests can be arranged on request; select public spaces may be open for wedding parties subject to availability; and exclusive use of one of four restaurants (Pelagos, Helios, Taverna 37, Mercato) is offered for private dining. Special linen colours and designs are available on request.

Melenos's separate weddings site (linked from the hotel's weddings page) names two ceremony locations at the hotel, the Blue Balcony and the Magical Garden, and also offers vow renewals, commitment ceremonies, baby naming ceremonies and anniversaries. It publishes no named package or inclusion list beyond the hotel weddings page.

Grand Resort Lagonissi's Weddings & Celebrations overview refers to 'special wedding packages' and 'exclusive wedding packages', says its wedding planner can tailor any wedding to the couple, and says its venues host weddings, receptions, christenings, galas and private events for up to 1,200 guests. It links a weddings brochure PDF dated 2022 (uploads/2022/07).
facts.conflicts: Overview gives events up to 1,200 guests (all event types); no per-venue wedding capacity on the Weddings & Ceremonies page.

facts.claim: Grand Resort Lagonissi's weddings brochure (PDF uploaded July 2022, linked from the live Weddings & Celebrations page) shows an on-site chapel, St Dimitrios; lists services including a personal wedding planner, DJs with sound and lighting, photography, bridal wear, wedding suits, favours, special effects, limousine rentals, chefs, pastry chefs and floral and table designers; says the resort 'returns their trust by offering them their stay as a gift' with a honeymoon suite for the wedding night (fruit, treats, breakfast in bed, champagne); and its enquiry form asks whether the ceremony is in a church, at the hotel or elsewhere. Seated capacities include Uranus and Cosmos Ballroom 600 buffet / 700 set menu, La Piscina 450 buffet, Veghera 300 / 350 and Aphrodite 260 / 300.
facts.conflicts: Brochure dates from 2022 and still gives fax contacts and grandresort.gr addresses; the live Weddings & Ceremonies page lists a similar service set but does not repeat the complimentary wedding-night stay. Treat the brochure terms as possibly superseded.

insider_details.detail: Package pages use the word loosely: Four Seasons Astir Palace lists ten named wedding inclusions, Melenos sends a costing sheet with deadlines, while Lagonissi, Costa Navarino, Corfu Imperial and Amanzoe give no inclusion list and work from a proposal. Ask every venue for its inclusions in writing before comparing.

Legal paperwork is not handled the same way everywhere: Melenos's coordinator files documents and registers the licence, Atrium Prestige assists civil couples to obtain the licence, and Angsana Corfu's 2026 brochure lists symbolic ceremony venues only. Ask which ceremony type the package is built for before signing.

Rooms can be a condition rather than an add-on: Melenos suggests taking the whole hotel for at least three nights, and Four Seasons' event specialists manage guest room blocks, so ask whether the package depends on a room commitment and for how many nights.

Seasonal venue windows shape the date: Angsana Corfu's Vertigo Sky Bar runs roughly late May to the end of September and Oribu Restaurant only in the shoulder months, and Smartraveller flags June to September wildfires and summer heatwaves, so ask for the weather back-up venue in writing.

Supplier rules differ: Four Seasons will work with the couple's own florist and its specialist works 'with you or your consultant', while others name in-house services; ask whether outside suppliers are allowed and on what terms.

Insurance is part of the package decision: Smartraveller says read the PDS, cover every stopover and check cancellation cover if the advice level rises after booking, and there is no free healthcare agreement with Greece. Line up policy cancellation terms against the venue's deposit terms.
